Prime Minister Mariano Rajoy of the People's Party (PP) spoke today at the upper house of Spanish legislative, the Senate building.

http://www.gomadrid.com/sights/palacio-senado.jpg

In the speech, he announced that, in closed door sessions over the last few months, the party leaders for the five main political parties have reached an agreement on the budget for the 2019 fiscal year. The extra $59 million dollars (51 million in Euros) in income from the [Sale of land to Liberland's marijuana growing process](https://voat.co/v/ModernPowers/comments/1012958), will be dedicated to improving conditions for the poor and average citizens of the nation; this is in addition to a new $2 billion stimulus package also announced which provides benefits to social programs as well as grants and stimulus to businesses both big and small. These were the Prime Minister's words -

https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/ea/Mariano_Rajoy_2015c_%28cropped%29.jpg

*"Today, the differing blocs and ideologies have reached a long-necessary and awaited agreement. We will show to the world how Spain cares for its citizens, and puts their well-being first and foremost. We will show the world a nation where everyone can be expected to succeed, everyone can be expected to be productive and industrious, and everyone can be expected to have a helping hand from both their private citizens and their government. In this way, our nation will continue to grow and be a leader in the EU as well as the world at large."*

*"In the spirit of co-operation, I want to make this point to the Spanish people as well. No matter what culture we hail from, what faith we call our own, or no matter our political leanings, one thing is certain: We are all as one. For many centuries, we have been united as a single union, a single people. We have been unique in our heritage in this way. We have united against common foes. We have suffered through civil wars, strife and famine, wars of aggression from foreign powers, and through it all, we have been stronger for it. We have come together in our hours of need, and we have been stronger for it. We reached out a hand to those less fortunate around the world, and we have been stronger for it."*

*"Today, we continue to face many issues. Many issues have split us into our various camps, and we reach a point where we refuse to debate; refuse to compromise. Today, the People's Party of Spain has shown that we are willing to debate; we are willing to compromise; we are willing to give in order to do what is right. And we will be stronger for it."*

The speech seems to be met with ambivalence overall, although a few people were supportive and many others think this might be a turnaround for the PP, which has not held a majority in the legislative branch since 2015. The stimulus package will contribute more to Spain's budget deficit, which has been [decreasing steadily over the last few years](http://www.tradingeconomics.com/spain/government-budget). That said, the hope for Prime Minister Rajoy is that improvements in the economy and stimulated business will bring in enough income to off-set the additional costs. It does appear that Spain should once against be in the black sometime in the 2020's.
